questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECTLY spelt form of the word meaning 'to provide lodging or space for someone'?

options.option_text: acommodate — to provide lodging for guests
accomodate — to provide lodging for guests
accommodate — to provide lodging for guests
accommodaate — to provide lodging for guests

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Accommodate' requires DOUBLE 'c' and DOUBLE 'm' — both interior consonants are doubled. Option A (acommodate) drops one 'c'; Option B (accomodate) drops one 'm'; Option D inserts a spurious extra 'a'. Memory hook: 'Accommodate has enough room — it needs two c's and two m's'. Another example: 'accommodation' follows the same double-c, double-m pattern and appears frequently in official notices.

questions.stem: The invigilator announced it was _____ to carry a valid admit card to the examination hall. Identify the CORRECTLY spelt word.

options.option_text: necesary — something required or essential
necessary — something required or essential
neccesary — something required or essential
neccessary — something required or essential

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Necessary' has exactly ONE 'c' and TWO 's' letters. Option A (necesary) has only one 's'; Options C and D incorrectly double the 'c'. Memory hook: 'one Collar and two Socks' (1c, 2s). Another example: 'necessarily' (the adverb) preserves the same 1c-2s rule and is equally high-frequency in SSC Reading Comprehension passages.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECTLY spelt word meaning 'an instance or event that takes place'?

options.option_text: occurrance — an event or incident that takes place
ocurrence — an event or incident that takes place
occurence — an event or incident that takes place
occurrence — an event or incident that takes place

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Occurrence' doubles BOTH 'c' and 'r' before the suffix '-ence'. Option A ends in '-rance' instead of '-rence'; Option B drops one 'c'; Option C drops one 'r'. Trick: like 'accommodate', this word demands two doubled consonants — 'occur' + double-r + 'ence'. Another example: 'recurrence' follows the identical double-r pattern and tests the same examiner trap.

questions.stem: The senior IAS officer was appointed as the official _____ between the district administration and the state secretariat. Choose the CORRECTLY spelt word.

options.option_text: liaison — an official link between two bodies
liason — an official link between two bodies
liasion — an official link between two bodies
liasson — an official link between two bodies

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Liaison' is spelt l-i-a-i-s-o-n — the critical sequence is 'i-a-i' in the middle. Option B (liason) omits the second 'i'; Option C (liasion) swaps the final 'i' and 'o'; Option D doubles the 's'. Etymology: borrowed from French, meaning 'a binding'. Another example: 'liaison officer' appears verbatim in SSC CGL administrative-passage questions and must be written with the double-i pattern.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECTLY spelt word meaning 'a special right or advantage granted to a particular person or group'?

options.option_text: privelege — a special right available to select few
priviledge — a special right available to select few
privilege — a special right available to select few
privilige — a special right available to select few

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Privilege' ends in '-lege', NOT '-ledge'. Option B (priviledge) wrongly inserts a 'd' by false analogy with 'knowledge'; Option A swaps 'e' and 'i' in the third syllable; Option D replaces the final 'e' with 'i'. Memory hook: 'Privilege has no ledge to stand on — drop the d'. Etymology: Latin 'privilegium' (private law). Another example: the adjective 'privileged' simply adds '-d' to the base, retaining the same '-lege' core.

questions.stem: The audit committee praised the accounts officer for being a _____ professional who verified each entry without exception. Identify the CORRECTLY spelt word.

options.option_text: consientious — painstakingly careful and thorough
conscientious — painstakingly careful and thorough
consciencious — painstakingly careful and thorough
conscientous — painstakingly careful and thorough

questions.explanation: B is correct. The word is built as con-sci-en-tious — the 'sci' cluster (as in 'science') sits at its core. Option A (consientious) drops the 'c' before 'i', breaking the 'sci' cluster; Option C (consciencious) inserts a spurious second 'c' after 'science'; Option D (conscientous) omits the 'i' before '-ous', a common syllable-swallowing error. Memory hook: 'conscientious contains SCIENCE inside it — con + SCIENCE + tious'. Another example: 'omniscient' uses the same Latin 'sci-' root, helping reinforce the cluster.

questions.stem: The research wing of the ministry distributed a detailed _____ to gather baseline data from five hundred households. Choose the CORRECTLY spelt word.

options.option_text: questionaire — a printed list of survey questions
questionairre — a printed list of survey questions
questionnare — a printed list of survey questions
questionnaire — a printed list of survey questions

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Questionnaire' has DOUBLE 'n' and ends in '-aire' (French suffix). Option A (questionaire) has only one 'n' and one 'r'; Option B (questionairre) correctly uses '-aire' but doubles the 'r' instead of the 'n'; Option C (questionnare) doubles 'n' correctly but omits the 'i' in the suffix '-aire'. Memory hook: 'questionnaire = question + n + aire — double the n like the word inn, then add French -aire as in millionaire'. Another example: 'millionaire' shares the identical '-aire' suffix and is tested in the same SSC spelling-test pattern.

questions.stem: The chairman exercised his casting vote, which is a _____ reserved exclusively for the presiding officer. Choose the correctly spelt option.

options.option_text: privilage reserved for the presiding officer
previliege reserved for the presiding officer
privilege reserved for the presiding officer
privelege reserved for the presiding officer

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Privilege' is spelt p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e. The most frequent error is 'privelege' (swapping 'i' and 'e' before 'g') or 'privilage' (substituting 'a' for the second 'e'). Memory hook: think of 'privi-LEGE' — a legal leg-up. Option B ('previliege') adds an extra 'ie' and misspells the prefix. Example: 'It is a privilege to address this august legislative body.'

questions.stem: The judge ruled that it was _____ for both parties to submit their affidavits within seven working days. Identify the correctly spelt word.

options.option_text: neccesary to comply with the court's order
necesary to comply with the court's order
necessary to comply with the court's order
neccessary to comply with the court's order

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Necessary' has exactly one 'c' and two 's' letters: n-e-c-e-s-s-a-r-y. Classic mnemonic: 'one Collar, two Socks' (1c, 2s). Option A ('neccesary') wrongly doubles the 'c'. Option B ('necesary') drops one 's'. Option D ('neccessary') doubles both 'c' and 's'. Example: 'Submission of a medical certificate is necessary for all leave applications under service rules.'

questions.stem: The meteorological department described the simultaneous flooding of three river basins as a rare _____. Which option gives the correct spelling?

options.option_text: occurance seen only in extreme monsoon years
occurrance seen only in extreme monsoon years
ocurrence seen only in extreme monsoon years
occurrence seen only in extreme monsoon years

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Occurrence' doubles both 'c' and 'r': o-c-c-u-r-r-e-n-c-e. Rule: the base verb 'occur' doubles its final consonant before a vowel suffix (occur → occurring → occurrence). Option A ('occurance') has correct double-c but uses wrong suffix '-ance' instead of '-ence'. Option B ('occurrance') has correct double-r but wrong suffix. Option C ('ocurrence') drops one 'c'. Example: 'The occurrence of simultaneous bank failures triggered a systemic review by RBI.'

questions.stem: Before the medical board cleared the applicants, each candidate had to fill a detailed health _____. Select the correctly spelt word.

options.option_text: questionnaire submitted at the examination centre
questionaire submitted at the examination centre
questionairre submitted at the examination centre
questionnairre submitted at the examination centre

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Questionnaire' = question + naire (French suffix): q-u-e-s-t-i-o-n-n-a-i-r-e. It has double 'n' and ends in '-aire' not '-air' or '-airre'. Option B ('questionaire') drops one 'n' — the single most common error at SSC level. Option C ('questionairre') retains one 'n' but doubles the 'r'. Option D ('questionnairre') doubles both 'n' and 'r'. Memory hook: 'QUESTION + NAIRE' — the extra 'n' belongs to the French suffix. Example: 'Applicants must complete the questionnaire before undergoing the physical fitness test.'

questions.stem: The new hostel complex was designed specifically to _____ differently-abled students with accessible ramps and wider corridors. Identify the correctly spelt word.

options.option_text: accomodate the differently-abled student cohort
acommodate the differently-abled student cohort
accomadate the differently-abled student cohort
accommodate the differently-abled student cohort

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Accommodate' has double 'c' AND double 'm': a-c-c-o-m-m-o-d-a-t-e. Option A ('accomodate') has correct double 'c' but only one 'm' — the most frequent error. Option B ('acommodate') has correct double 'm' but only one 'c'. Option C ('accomadate') changes the second 'o' to 'a'. Memory hook: 'ACC-OMMO-DATE' — two c's for two colleagues, two m's for two mattresses. Example: 'The new conference hall can accommodate up to 400 delegates comfortably.'

questions.stem: The officer was designated to act as _____ between the Ministry of External Affairs and the United Nations field mission. Which option is correctly spelt?

options.option_text: liaison between two high-level diplomatic bodies
liaision between two high-level diplomatic bodies
liasion between two high-level diplomatic bodies
liasson between two high-level diplomatic bodies

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Liaison' is spelt l-i-a-i-s-o-n — the unusual 'iaiso' cluster makes this one of the hardest SSC spelling items. It derives from French 'lier' (to bind). Option B ('liaision') inserts an extra 'i' after 's'. Option C ('liasion') transposes 'a' and 's', the most common confusion. Option D ('liasson') incorrectly doubles the 's'. Memory hook: read it as 'LI–AI–SON' — the string 'ai' appears twice before the 's'. Example: 'The defence attaché served as liaison between Army headquarters and the civilian administration.'

questions.stem: A probationary IPS officer must be _____ while recording witness statements, as even a minor clerical lapse can render evidence inadmissible in court. Select the correctly spelt word.

options.option_text: conscientous in recording every procedural detail
concientious in recording every procedural detail
consciencious in recording every procedural detail
conscientious in recording every procedural detail

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Conscientious' is spelt c-o-n-s-c-i-e-n-t-i-o-u-s. It contains the word 'science' at its core (Latin 'scientia' = knowledge). Option A ('conscientous') drops the 'i' before '-ous' — an extremely subtle error. Option B ('concientious') omits the first 's' after 'con'. Option C ('consciencious') inserts an extra 'c', conflating 'conscience' with 'conscientious'. Memory hook: spot 'con-SCIENCE-tious' — the word science lives inside it. Example: 'A conscientious civil servant never approves a file without reading every noting carefully.'
